text:
sarah: Quick heads-up — our onboarding sample app (FastAPI) instructs folks to instantiate AsyncClient at module import. On hot-reload or local dev I keep hitting "RuntimeError: Event loop is closed" during shutdown. Repro steps below.

mike: Oof. Can you paste the minimal snippet?

sarah: Sure — this is what the guide shows right now:
```py
# app/main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient()  # created at import time
app = FastAPI()

@app.get('/')
async def root():
    return await client.generate('hi')
```

sarah: Start with `uvicorn --reload` and edit any file to trigger reload, then CTRL+C. On shutdown I see:
```
ERROR: Exception in callback BaseEventLoop.call_soon
handle: <Handle cancelled>
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
```

jen: This is a classic lifespan-on-import issue. Creating async clients at import time ties them to the first loop; reload spawns a new loop and closing the old one leaves attached handles.

raul: Workarounds: 1) create client in startup event and store on `app.state` 2) use an `async with AsyncClient()` inside route (less ideal) 3) ensure client implements a sync-safe lazy init.

mike: Can we improve the sample guide text to show the startup pattern? Also we should consider making our Python SDK AsyncClient lazy-init so import-time creation is not footgun.

sarah: Agreed — will send a tiny docs PR. But there's also a bug: even if you do `await client.aclose()` on shutdown, some `httpx` internals leak tasks bound to the first loop. Repro attached.

jen: Can you share the exact httpx version? We've seen this with older httpx/anyio combos.

sarah: httpx==0.24.0, anyio==4.0.0. Full trace shows `Task was destroyed but it is pending!` referencing `asyncio.create_task` inside `httpcore`.

raul: Two angles: short-term docs + sample fix, long-term SDK change. I propose we add a context-manager-friendly wrapper and a module-level warning in __init__ to discourage import-time instantiation. Also a lint rule in sample templates.

mike: For the SDK change: implement AsyncClient.__init__ to accept `lazy=True` which delays creating the httpx client/loop-bound resources until first await. That would mitigate this class of bug. Anyone worried about breaking behavior?

jen: Sounds reasonable. We should preserve current semantics by default, or else bump major. `lazy=True` opt-in is safe. Also add a deprecation warning in docs for import-time usage.

sarah: I'll open two PRs: (1) docs/sample change; (2) SDK lazy-init prototype. Linking when ready.

sarah: PR for docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/422

mike: Thanks. For QA: please add a tiny pytest that runs `uvicorn` or simulates reload, plus an integration test that checks `Task was destroyed` absence. We should run that in CI matrix against multiple anyio/httpx versions.

ci-bot: CI pipeline queued for branch sarah/async-client-lazy-init — matrices: py3.10/3.11 x httpx 0.24/0.25 x anyio 3/4

raul: One more thought — mention this in onboarding email; folks often copy-paste the quickstart. A short callout like "do not create AsyncClient at module import" would save time.

mike: Agreed. I'll draft a one-paragraph note for the onboarding doc.

sarah: Cool. I'll follow up with PR links and a short reproduction gist. Thanks all :thumbsup:
